sections.title: Overview
sections.body: The Project Workbench is the primary workspace for Project Leads. It uses a master-detail layout: a project list on the left and a three-tab workspace on the right. You can also arrive here via deep links from Portfolio Overview.

sections.title: Project List
sections.body:
The left panel shows projects filtered by your role. Project Leads see their assigned projects; Controllers see all. Each entry shows the project name, RAG indicator, type badge, and next action due. Projects in Draft or Pending Approval status also appear for PLs with appropriate status badges.

Use the **New** button at the top to create a new project draft. The creation form collects project name, description, organizational entity (e.g., Line of Business), CapEx/OpEx classification, start/end months, and optional resource plan allocation.

sections.title: Overview Tab
sections.body: Shows project metadata (name, hierarchy path, status, RAG, timeline), the 3-point comparison table (Baseline vs Current Forecast vs Actuals with variance columns), a monthly trajectory line chart (three lines showing baseline, forecast, and actuals over time), CapEx/OpEx breakdown, and resource plan summary.

sections.title: 3-Point Comparison
sections.body: The comparison table shows three rows (Baseline, Current Forecast, Actuals) broken out by internal hours, external costs, and total. Variance columns show Plan Drift (forecast vs baseline), Execution Variance (actuals vs forecast), and Total Variance (actuals vs baseline). This gives a complete picture of where the project stands.

sections.title: Forecast & Planning Tab
sections.body: In read mode, shows the current forecast grid with months as columns and resource roles + external cost types as rows. To edit, start a Monthly Review cycle which walks through 5 phases: Retrospective, System Suggestions, Editing, Review, and Submit.

sections.title: Monthly Forecast Wizard
sections.body:
**Phase 1 (Retrospective):** Review last month's forecast vs actuals and acknowledge variances. All monetary values are shown in full EUR format (e.g. 2.720 €). **Phase 2 (Suggestions):** System shows AI-generated insights based on trends, burn rates, and utilization patterns. Apply or dismiss each suggestion. **Phase 3 (Editing):** Edit the forecast grid directly — both hours and external costs. If no changes are needed, use the 'Keep as is' button to proceed without modifications. **Phase 4 (Review):** See all changes grouped by category with old/new/delta values in full EUR format. Add justification text. **Phase 5 (Submit):** Changes become CRs routed to the Controller for review. The Controller can approve, reject, or request changes with an editable grid.

**Forecast Locking:** While a CR is pending review (at any stage — controller, CC Owner, or sent back for changes), the Rolling Forecast Review button is disabled with a status indicator showing the CR number and its current approval stage. This prevents overlapping CRs for the same project.

sections.title: Change History Tab
sections.body:
Shows the chronological log of all change requests for this project. Each CR row displays its status badge, category, summary, cost impact, timestamp, submitter, and whether it was system-suggested.

**Sent-Back CRs:** Change requests returned by the controller are highlighted with an amber border, amber background, a warning icon, and an 'Action Required' badge. Expanding a sent-back CR shows an inline diff view instead of the normal grid.

**Diff View for Sent-Back CRs:** When the controller has requested changes, expanding the CR reveals:
- **Controller Feedback** banner (amber) with the controller's comments explaining why changes were made
- **KPI Strip** showing Affected Lines (Current), Affected Lines (Proposed), and Total Impact
- **Color-coded comparison grid** with collapsible year columns: green cells for reductions, red for increases, blue for other changes. Each changed cell shows the original value (strikethrough) above the proposed value.
- **Legend** explaining the color coding
- **Accept Changes** button — applies the controller's proposed values and advances the CR (to CC Owner if resource changes, or directly to approved)
- **Decline and Resubmit** button — resets the CR back to pending_controller_approval for the PL to resubmit with their own modifications

**Normal CRs:** Non-sent-back CRs expand to show a tabular detail view grid with monthly comparison data, KPI strip, justification, and a 'View Full Detail' button.

sections.title: System Suggestions
sections.body: The system analyzes spending patterns and generates suggestions during the forecast wizard. Types include trend-based adjustments, burn rate projections, actuals-based corrections, and utilization insights. System-suggested changes are flagged in the resulting CR for controller transparency.

sections.title: Project Submission Workflow
sections.body:
New projects follow a multi-step submission lifecycle:

**1. Create Draft:** Project Lead clicks 'New' in the project list, fills in project details and an optional resource plan with monthly hour allocations. The project is saved as 'draft' status.

**2. Submit for Review:** PL clicks 'Submit' to send the draft for CC Owner confirmation. The forecast snapshot is saved as the 'original' submission. Status becomes 'pending_cc_confirmation'.

**3. CC Owner Confirmation:** The CC Owner reviews and confirms resource availability. Status moves to 'pending_approval'.

**4. Controller Review:** The controller reviews the submission in the Portfolio Overview Intake Queue. They can Approve (project becomes active), Reject (back to draft), or Request Changes (opens editable forecast grid to propose modifications).

**5. Changes Requested:** If the controller requests changes, the PL sees an amber banner in the Workbench with the controller's feedback. The PL can 'Review Proposed Changes' to see a diff view, then 'Accept Changes' or 'Edit and Resubmit'.

sections.title: Changes Requested Banner
sections.body:
When a controller requests changes to a submitted project, the Project Lead sees an amber notification banner at the top of the project workspace. The banner shows the controller's feedback text and provides two actions:

- **Review Proposed Changes** — opens a diff view comparing the PL's original submission against the controller's proposed changes, with changed cells highlighted
- **Edit and Resubmit** — opens the forecast grid for the PL to make their own adjustments before resubmitting

The same diff view is also accessible from the Intake Queue in Portfolio Overview by clicking 'Open Full Detail' on a project with 'changes_requested' status.

sections.title: Change Request Workflow
sections.body:
Change requests follow a multi-step lifecycle:

**1. PL Submits CR:** During the monthly forecast review, the Project Lead submits changes that become a CR with status 'pending_controller_approval'. While the CR is pending, the forecast review button is locked to prevent overlapping submissions.

**2. Controller Review:** The Controller sees pending CRs in the Portfolio Overview CR Approvals tab. They can:
- **Approve** — CR is approved. If it has internal resource changes, it routes to the CC Owner for confirmation first.
- **Reject** — CR is rejected with a reason.
- **Request Changes** — Controller opens an editable grid to adjust specific values (hours, amounts) and sends back with feedback.

**3. PL Reviews Changes (if sent back):** The PL sees the sent-back CR in their Change History with an amber 'Action Required' badge. Expanding it shows a diff view comparing original vs controller-proposed values with color-coded cells. The PL can:
- **Accept Changes** — applies the controller's proposed values
- **Decline and Resubmit** — resets CR to pending_controller_approval

**4. CC Owner Confirmation (if resource changes):** When a CR with internal resource changes is approved (by controller or PL accepting changes), delta-based resource requests are created for the CC Owner. Each request shows the change direction (increase or decrease), the delta hours (not the absolute total), the original allocation, the resulting total, and who is currently allocated to that role. The CC Owner can confirm, partially fulfill, counter-propose, or decline. For increases, new allocation hours are added; for decreases, existing allocations are reduced. Confirmation completes the CR and updates the forecast.

**Final state:** Approved CRs update the project's forecast data. The full audit trail is visible in the Change History tab.
